ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 cancellation fee; no refund or account action. Optionally remind the driver that the "I'm Here" tap is recorded from the moment of the tap onwards.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show case, so it enters the cancellation-fee rules through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver with the driver asserting the rider no-show [F4][F12][NS-0]. The fee on record is $5.00, not the $6.61 default, and the case record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes (≥ 8:00), so NS-1's (iii) is applied with those case-record parameters rather than the 3-minute default [F4][F7][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met: arrival was confirmed by a driver tap, not a platform auto-decision — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:17:10 [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) is met: at the moment of that tap the driver was 39 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius (his closest approach overall was 6 m at 12:16:45) [F1][F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (iii) is met under the case record's threshold: he remained continuously within 200 m for 490 s after the tap, which is ≥ the 480 s (8 min) threshold, and he cancelled at 12:25:20 [F3][F5][F6][NS-1]. The trace confirms the GPS samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold, so the continued wait is not being inferred between samples [F2][F6][NS-1].

The rider's account is that by the time she came out the driver had already cancelled and she was charged $5.00 anyway [F4][F7]. That does not defeat the fee, because NS-1 does not require the rider to be present, only that the three conditions on the driver's side hold; and the driver did message "At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel" at 12:17 and only announced the cancellation at 12:25 after the wait was up [F9][F10][NS-1]. The rider's side is left to the NS-7 human-appeal route rather than an automatic refund.

Safety screen: I read every chat message, the driver's statement, the complaint and the timeline. The chat is a pickup notice and a cancellation notice, the statement is a factual no-show explanation, and the complaint is a fee objection [F9][F10][F12][F4]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere in these materials; the only other facts are traffic band and weather data [F13][F15][SAFE-1]. Nothing here triggers SAFE-1 or SAFE-2, so the case can be decided on the ordinary cancellation rules.

Evidence is sufficient: the complaint, the chat and the timeline all lie within the trip window, every chat message is timestamped, and the GPS trace fully covers the wait with no hole, so every element NS-0/NS-1 needs is settled by a record [F1][F2][F4][F6][F11]. No refund flows from the route-deviation rules either, and there is no ERP or toll field here, so no amount is owed; the amount is therefore null [F7][RD-2][FARE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Rider advocate's request for no_action is granted in outcome, but the rider-side assertion in the complaint that she was charged the fee despite coming out is not a ground to waive it: NS-1 turns on the driver-side conditions, all of which hold — arrival confirmed by driver tap at 12:17:10, 39 m from pickup, and 490 s ≥ the case-record 480 s (8 min) wait threshold, with the GPS trace covering the wait without a gap [F2][F3][F6][F11][NS-1].

The complaint's premise that the $5.00 charge was unjustified is rejected on the record: the fee equals the case-record cancellation fee [F4][F7], and NS-0/NS-1 make it payable where the driver taps I'm Here at the pickup and waits past the threshold, which the trace settles with a complete, hole-free GPS record [F2][F6][NS-1]. Any hardship is a matter for the NS-7 appeal, not an automatic refund.

The driver's statement that he 'waited the full 8 minutes' after pressing I'm Here is accepted in substance, but the correct window is measured from the tap at 12:17:10 to cancellation at 12:25:20 = 490 s, not from acceptance; the earlier stationary period from 12:16:50 is outside the measured window and is not counted in (iii) [F3][F5][F6][NS-1].

No account flag is warranted on these facts: NS-1 (i)-(iii) all hold so NS-2's flag trigger (arrival pressed while outside the pickup radius) does not arise, and RD-6's repeated-deviation flag is not reached because there is no route deviation and no refund in this case [F1][F6][NS-2][RD-6].
